asr_text: The disagreement is not really about movement; it is about where stability comes from. One employee finds it in a desk that stays put, with papers and a familiar start. The other finds it in the power to change social distance and the kind of space needed that day. A shared-seat system can even create unofficial regular desks, so a rule that looks flexible on paper may feel like friction to one person, while the same system feels useful to another.
